jobs.description:
A Snapshot of Your Day 

As a Commodity Manager (f/m/d) CD & NUC, you will shape the sourcing strategy for some of Siemens Energy’s most advanced technology categories, including electronic equipment, controls, digitalization, and nuclear services. Working closely with engineering, quality, and project teams, you will build resilient supplier partnerships, negotiate complex commercial agreements, and ensure a secure, cost-effective supply chain that supports global business growth.

How You’ll Make an Impact 

* Develop and execute global sourcing and category strategies for electronic equipment, controls, and digital technologies
* Identify, evaluate, and onboard strategic suppliers through market analysis, spend optimization, and cross-functional collaboration
* Build long-term partnerships with key suppliers while driving performance through KPIs, business reviews, and continuous improvement initiatives
* Lead supplier development programs to strengthen quality, capability, and supply chain resilience in technically complex and regulated environments
* Negotiate complex commercial contracts, including pricing, intellectual property, and long-term service agreements, to maximize value and minimize risk
* Proactively assess supply chain risks and implement mitigation strategies to ensure business continuity across global procurement activities

What You Bring

* Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Engineering, Economics or a comparable technical or business discipline
* Extensive experience in strategic procurement, sourcing, or category management with a strong focus on electronic equipment and technical commodities
* Proven expertise in managing complex supplier relationships, supplier development, and procurement projects within regulated or high-technology industries
* Strong commercial acumen with advanced contract negotiation, contract management, and risk mitigation capabilities
* Analytical and strategic mindset with excellent stakeholder management skills; knowledge of AI applications and procurement automation is a plus
* Business fluent in German and English

About the Team

Our Gas Services division offers Low-emission power generation through service and decarbonization. Zero or low emission power generation and all gas turbines under one roof, steam turbines and generators. Decarbonization opportunities through service offerings, modernization, and digitalization of the fleet.

Who is Siemens Energy? 

At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With ~100.000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. The technologies created in our research departments and factories drive the energy transition and provide the base for one sixth of the world's electricity generation.

Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation.      

Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Energy: https://www.siemens-energy.com/employeevideo

Our Commitment to Diversity 

Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by over 130 nationalities. Siemens Energy celebrates character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences. 

Rewards/Benefits 

* In addition to an attractive remuneration package in line with the market, you can expect an attractive employer-financed company pension scheme
* We also offer the opportunity to become a Siemens Energy shareholder
* We offer our employees the opportunity to work flexibly and remotely, and our inspiring offices provide space for collaboration and creativity
* The professional and personal development of our employees is very important to us. We provide them with the opportunities to learn and develop in a self-determined way, various attractive programmes and learning materials are available for this purpose
* In relation to the "compatibility of family and work", we have a wide range of offers, e.g. flexible working time models, childcare places at many locations, the possibility of trial part-time work or even a sabbatical  

We value equal opportunities and welcome applications from people with disabilities.

jobs.description:
Scientist – Quantum Sensors & Qubit Technology (m/f/d)

The Semiconductor Laboratory (HLL) of the Max Planck Society, located on the research campus in Garching near Munich, is a leading facility for the development of highly precise radiation sensors and detector systems. On approximately 1,400 m² of cleanroom space, HLL develops, fabricates and tests advanced semiconductor detectors for applications in X-ray astronomy, particle physics and materials research. With around 50 employees from different nationalities, HLL provides a highly international and interdisciplinary environment in which scientists, engineers and technology specialists work closely together across the entire development chain — from fundamental research and simulation to device design, fabrication and experimental characterization.

To strengthen our activities in quantum sensing and advanced quantum-device technologies, and to provide scientific and technological support to our research, engineering and service teams, we are looking for a Scientist – Quantum Sensors & Qubit Technology (m/f/d) to join our team at the earliest possible date on a full-time basis (39 hours/week). 

Your responsibilities

- Develop and optimize quantum sensor concepts based on qubit systems and quantum effects.
- Perform advanced numerical simulations and modeling of qubit-based sensing systems, including relevant physical processes, noise sources and system-level performance.
- Work closely with technology development, engineering and experimental teams to translate simulation results into practical implementations.
- Analyze experimental data and use the results to refine physical models and sensor designs.
- Contribute to scientific publications, technical documentation and intellectual property.

Your profile

- PhD in physics, electrical engineering, applied physics, quantum engineering or a related field.
- Background in quantum sensing, qubit control and precision measurement.
- Experience with numerical simulation, modeling and system design.
- Analytical and problem-solving skills combined with a practical, technology-oriented mindset.
- Strong motivation to work in close cooperation with technology, engineering and experimental teams.
- Fluency in English; knowledge of German is an advantage.

Advantageous experience

Experience in one or more of the following areas would be particularly valuable:

- Cleanroom / semiconductor / microfabrication experience
- Familiarity with Python, MATLAB, COMSOL or equivalent 
- MEMS/NEMS or integrated sensor technologies
- Precision measurement and low-noise instrumentation
- Experience bridging qubit physics, device design and fabrication technology

What we offer

- International environment, diverse responsibilities and a high degree of autonomy: Flat hierarchies and a collaborative, agile team within an internationally renowned research institution. You will work closely with scientists, engineers and technology specialists across disciplines and have the opportunity to shape the development of innovative quantum-sensing technologies.
- Advantages of the public sector: Remuneration according to the German public service pay scale TVöD (Bund), depending on qualifications and experience; occupational pension scheme (VBL); 30 days of annual leave (31 days as of 2027), plus additional days off on Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve. The position is initially limited to two years, with the possibility of subsequent permanent employment.
- Work-life balance and compatibility of family and career: Flexible working hours (flextime), opportunities for mobile working, support in finding childcare and care for family members, and a comprehensive company health management program.
- Professional development: Thorough onboarding and opportunities for internal and external training and further education tailored to your individual needs. You will have the opportunity to continuously develop your expertise in quantum sensing, qubit technology, simulation and semiconductor technology.
- Research campus: Excellent access by public transport, including the possibility of a monthly subsidy for the “Deutschland-Job-Ticket”, or by car with free parking in the immediate vicinity of the laboratory. A canteen and further dining options are available nearby, as well as campus-wide events and activities.

The Max Planck Society strives for gender equality and diversity. The Max Planck Society is committed to increasing the number of individuals with disabilities in its workforce and therefore encourages applications from such qualified individuals. Furthermore, the Max Planck Society seeks to increase the number of women in those areas where they are underrepresented and therefore explicitly encourages women to apply.

Further information and application

Detailed information about the Semiconductor Laboratory (HLL) can be found at HLL – Semiconductor Laboratory (http://www.hll.mpg.de/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) .

For further information about the position, please contact Dr. Jelena Ninkovic, Tel.: +49 89 839400-49.

Please submit your application, including meaningful application documents, exclusively online via our application portal (https://bewerbermanagement.net/en/jobposting/6c80f90f47c14e1b28b7c86e27f035140c44c8f20/apply) by 31 October 2026. Include the names of three referees that can be contacted in your CV.

jobs.occupation: BTA, MTA oder CTA (m/f/d) – CG-2026-2 (Biologisch-technische/r Assistent/in)
jobs.description:
The LIT - Leibniz Institute for Immunotherapy (foundation under civil law) (https://lit.eu/) – is a biomedical research center focusing on translational immunology in the fields of cancer immunotherapy, transplant rejection and autoimmunity. The objective of the LIT is to develop innovative and efficient cellular immune therapeutics in these areas. Our own GMP laboratories and close networking with University and University Hospital offer excellent opportunities for clinical translation of novel immune cell products.

The Flow Cytometry Core Facility is recruiting a highly motivated

BTA, MTA oder CTA (m/f/d) – CG-2026-2

(full time, 40.1 hours per week)

The position is initially limited to two years with the possibility of extension.

The Flow Cytometric Cell Analytics and Cell Sorting Core Facility at the LIT offers research groups from the LIT, the University Hospital of Regensburg (UKR), and the University of Regensburg (UR) the opportunity to identify and characterize individual cell populations and to isolate them in a targeted manner, thus making them accessible for further downstream analysis. In addition, the facility offers advice and support for beginners and advanced users on flow cytometry-related questions and problems, such as the selection of appropriate fluorochromes, the creation of staining panels and the optimization of gating strategies.

We are now looking for a highly motivated technical assistant with excitement for flow cytometry, sophisticated instruments, organizational/administrative skills and a stong service mentality who is excited to enrich our facility. The facility hosts state-of-the art sorters and analyzers. The community of users is highly international and covers a range of scientific topics within and associated with Immunology.

Your tasks include, but are not limited to:

- Daily operation of the sorting machines
- Monitor and maintain the equipment in the facility, including arriving spectral cytometers. This includes quality control and cleaning of equipment.
- Reagent and consumables management, including planning, tracking and ordering of reagents and preparation of solutions and reagents
- Documentation, SOP and data management, including tracking and recording of instrument usage per user, creating and updating protocols for instruments, data backup and transfer to sorter users
- User support, including assisting users with scheduling of experiments, training experienced users for independent equipment usage of sorting machines and their software, expert advice to users
- Support for research initiatives of the facility, e.g. assisting flow cytometry-related research projects, assay development, promote the facility’s scientific work
- Management of facility waste, including autoclaving and coordination of waste disposal
- Ensure smooth operation of the facility

The ideal candidate possesses:

- Completed education as BTA, MTA or CTA
- Experience in handling of live cells, advanced equipment, flow cytometry
- High affinity for and ideally experience with work with sophisticated equipment, incuding equipment maintenance and trouble-shooting
- Experience in providing training
- Self-motivated person with an intrinsic service mentality, a collaborative attitude and the drive to advance the research within the institute
- Reliable and precise work style, high degree of independence
- Good organizational and administrative skills
- Good inter-personal skills, good communication skills in English and German
- Interest, and ideally also experience in working in an interdisciplinary and international environment

We offer:

- An international cutting-edge research environment that offers exciting and diverse opportunities
- Flat hierarchies and short decision-making processes
- A highly motivated and cooperative team
- Flexible working hours
- Job ticket and excellent benefits
- Excellent funding situation and state-of-the-art equipment

The remuneration is based on TV-L.

The Leibniz Institute for Immunotherapy aims to increase the share of women in the workforce. Therefore, qualified female candidates are explicitly encouraged to submit their applications. Moreover, the LIT advocates for the compatibility of family and career.

Disabled applicants (m/f/d) with equal qualifications will receive preferential treatment within the recruitment procedure. Please refer to your disability status already in your application.

Please note that expenses that may arise in the context of an eventual job interview cannot be reimbursed.

For more information, please contact Prof. Dr. Carmen Gerlach (carmen.gerlach@lit.eu). We are looking forward to receiving your detailed application in German or English. Please apply via our Online - Application Portal (https://rci.hr4you.org/job/view/113/bta-mta-oder-cta-m-f-d-cg-2026-2?page_lang=en) the reference CG- 2026-2.

Application deadline is October 11th 2026.

- Provide user and customer feedback to IT on Tesla tools/systems and to Operations on processes

- Strong understanding of residential/small commercial energy storage, ideally including three-phase (3P) systems, hybrid inverters, and grid-tied architectures common in Germany
